The number of stars per unit range of parallax scales as the derivative of the cumulative number of stars with respect to parallax. Assuming stars are uniformly distributed in space (constant number density), the cumulative number of stars out to distance \(r\) is proportional to the volume: \(N(<r) \propto r^3\). Since parallax \(p \propto 1/r\), we have \(r \propto 1/p\), so \(N(<p) \propto p^{-3}\). Differentiating with respect to \(p\) gives \(dN/dp \propto p^{-4}\). Therefore, the number of stars per unit parallax range varies as \(1/\text{plx}^4\).

Answer: C
